items.headline: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
items.blurb: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
items.text: Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel, Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. items.headline: UK police open sex offence probe into comedian and author David Walliams
items.blurb: The British TV personality, 55, denies sexual assault allegations, saying he has not broken the law.
items.text: London’s police have opened an investigation into allegations of serious sexual offences after media reports accused British comedian and children’s author David Walliams of grooming and sexually abusing girls and young women. The Metropolitan Police said in a statement on Friday that it “has received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s”. In the statement, Met Police Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney urged anyone affected to come forward. The Met said the new allegations are separate from those reported this week by ITV News and The Guardian. The two news organisations published reports on Tuesday that several women had accused Walliams of sexual misconduct, with the allegations dating back as far as 2003. The reports came out a day after comedian Russell Brand was sentenced to more than 10 years in jail for rape and sexual assault. The Guardian and ITV said they spoke to more than 100 people during a three-year investigation. items.text: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter , which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October. Five days later, the Atlantic published an article titled “Yet another literary prize winner seems to be AI”, in which the author and journalist Vauhini Vara said the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated. The Caine prize chair, Ellah Wakatama, said in a statement : “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human-written. items.headline: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
items.blurb: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
items.text: Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world. Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover. The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide. Microsoft said it was a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or artificial intelligence agents. Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers. Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday. By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America. items.headline: Afghanistan’s new road to China ends at a closed border
items.blurb: Taliban government hopes its Wakhan Corridor road will open new trade routes and reduce reliance on Pakistan.
items.text: At an altitude of nearly 4,900 metres, at the Wakhjir Pass, Afghanistan ends and China begins. Snow closes the pass for at least five months of the year, and people cross it only sporadically in the months when it is passable. There is no official border crossing here, and yet, on October 4, Afghanistan’s Taliban-led government celebrated the opening of a road leading to the frontier – but crucially not crossing it. Afghanistan’s Ministry of Rural Rehabilitation and Development said the road through the Wakhan Corridor in Badakhshan province had been built in two phases for 365 million afghanis ($5.5m). It is a basic road – an unpaved track covered with gravel. On the other side of the border, there is no Chinese customs facility, and China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has not commented on the road’s opening. For the moment, the road leads to a closed border, with no indication of when Beijing might open it to commercial traffic. items.blurb: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
items.text: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways. items.text: The Delhi high court has ordered an expert review of four answers in the answer key for the examination to select candidates for UGC -Net June 2026, observing that errors in the answer key can impact a candidate’s merit ranking and eligibility. The examination, UGC-NET was conducted between June 22 to June 30, and approximately 7,27,506 candidates appeared for it, the results of which were declared in August, this year. A bench of justice Jasmeet Singh in his November 5 verdict, released on Thursday directed the expert committee to decide on the matter in three weeks, saying that the answer key appeared to contain errors. “An error of this kind should not be suffered by the candidates. A wrong key in a competitive examination affects ranking and eligibility, since the marks awarded on the basis of the key determine a candidate’s merit position and whether the candidate crosses the qualifying cut-off, and even a single mark may decide whether a candidate is considered,” the court said. According to a Lok Bhawan note, the controversy arose after Choudhary sought for lien or leave without pay a day after he joined as the assistant professor on February 17. The matter was presented for approval before the University Syndicate on August 19, which was declined citing provisions of the Bihar State Universities’ Act, 1976. items.headline: China's BYD clears import hurdle, looks to accelerate India push
items.blurb: Homologation removes the 2,500-unit import restriction on three models, giving the Chinese carmaker more room to scale its EV business as it enters the luxury market with Denza.
items.text: MUMBAI/NEW DELHI: BYD India has secured regulatory certification for three of its four models, removing the annual 2,500-unit import restriction on those vehicles and giving the Chinese carmaker greater flexibility to meet demand. The move is particularly significant for its fast-selling Sealion 7, as BYD seeks to expand its presence in India's electric passenger vehicle market. "We have four models and three of them are homologated with a certified agency, ARAI, except for Seal," Rajeev Chauhan, executive vice-president at BYD India, told Mint on the sidelines of the launch of the company's luxury brand Denza on Friday. Homologation is the process through which testing agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) certify that a vehicle meets the country's technical and safety requirements for road use. Under India's import rules, vehicles with international certification but without Indian homologation can be imported only up to 2,500 units per model annually. Securing Indian homologation removes that restriction. items.headline: Mars bets on India as a top-five growth market, targets $1.2 billion-plus revenue by 2030
items.blurb: The pet-care and snacking giant is expanding manufacturing and investing in technology capabilities as it looks to tap India's growing consumer markets and build a global operating hub.
items.text: HYDERABAD: Mars Inc., the American pet-care and snacking giant, wants India to become one of its five key “rapid growth” markets, betting on the country's expanding snacking and pet-care businesses to drive a sharp increase in revenue. India, already among Mars's top 20 markets, has significant room to grow, with the company targeting revenue of more than $1.2 billion by 2030. “It really ought to be a top 5 market,” Claus Aagaard, global chief financial officer of Mars, told Mint in an interview. The company's India revenue stood at around $600 million in 2025. Mars is stepping up investments in manufacturing and technology to capture that opportunity. It operates seven factories in India and is investing ₹ 1,500 crore in its Hyderabad pet-food facility. It has also partnered with IT services company Genpact to establish a global capability centre (GCC) in the city, which will support technology, analytics and process management across its global operations. “This is a new strategic investment for us to drive innovation around technology and process management,” Aagaard said on the sidelines of the GCC launch.

items.text: NEW YORK, Nov 13 (Reuters) - US stocks were lower on Friday, as concerns about Nvidia pressured technology shares, while a reading on inflation failed to alter expectations for more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve. Nvidia's shares fell 2.2% and were poised for their sixth straight week of declines, their longest streak since October 2012, after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday, following revelations of his relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for Beijing. The Financial Times reported that Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang. The uncertainty about leadership at the chipmaker has raised concerns about the durability of the AI trade, given Nvidia's primary role in the industry's boom and its financial ties to several companies in the sector, which has been a pillar of the bull market in equities. items.text: Listing the details of everything for sale everywhere is meant to make Amazon more useful than Reddit for people and AI agents.﻿ Listing the details of everything for sale everywhere is meant to make Amazon more useful than Reddit for people and AI agents.﻿ Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn’t sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters . The project, called the “World Product Graph,” is meant to make it less likely that shoppers leave Amazon to do their product research on Reddit or Google, and make it more likely shoppers end up at Amazon even if they’re searching for a product sold elsewhere. The same goes for AI agents — if Amazon has the largest stockpile of shopping data, AI agents may rely on its index of products over others, so even people shopping with bots will end up on its pages. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment. “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10. items.text: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces “fabricated claims” by more than 5x, according to Google’s analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash’s score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Google believes Hydrogen will be a key part of how developers work with agentic coding tools. items.text: Normally, the products I test don’t offer to help me write up my experience with them. Duet is different. Claude Duet is Anthropic’s AI agent for consumers, the latest attempt by an AI company to try to convince us that agents can be useful for people who don’t write code. It’s been an interesting couple of months: Instinct gave us an impressive text-based assistant , Meta offered us its cute little guy, Muse, to help us buy things , and OpenAI gave us the more work-oriented Dots . Claude Duet is even more focused on work than those. It’s also more consumer-friendly than Claude Cowork , which was more consumer-friendly than Claude Code — the coding agent that kicked off a whole hype cycle earlier this year. I’ve been testing it over the past week as I navigate a busy travel and work schedule. At turns it has been truly useful, kind of a nag, and very eager to write about itself. items.text: As companies look to accelerate innovation with artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and advanced modeling, the primary challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. items.text: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news. Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor , pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital. Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. “Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch. items.headline: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
items.blurb: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially…
items.text: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.”

items.text: As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape. Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ. It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures.” It’s a culture war, in other words. But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play a key role in setting federal AI policy. items.text: CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried. In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!” Called to action by a nonprofit grassroots advocacy group, the Illinois Families for Public Schools (ILFPS),

items.headline: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.blurb: LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith.
items.text: Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday. That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago , led by IVP. LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence. items.text: MeitY has sought details from Pronto, Snabbit and Urban Company on their collection and use of gig workers’ video and sensor data for physical AI training The move highlights growing government concerns around worker consent, consumer privacy, data security and the transfer of Indian training data to overseas AI developers The ministry has sought information on companies’ data collection SOPs and consent safeguards, as India’s physical AI data ecosystem expands The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has sought details from home services platforms, including Pronto, Snabbit and Urban Company’s InstaHelp, over the collection of first-person video and sensor data from gig workers for training physical AI models. As per a report by ET , a meeting chaired by MeitY secretary S Krishnan yesterday brought together senior executives from the quick home services platforms and other technology and robotics companies to discuss concerns around workers’ consent, consumer privacy and data sovereignty. Officials are concerned that recordings of everyday household activities could infringe workers’ rights, compromise consumer privacy and pose risks to national data security.
